overview: This file traces Japanese labor policy from wartime mobilization through the early U.S. occupation. Reports, laws, directives, correspondence, and translations document working conditions, union organizing, strikes, police conduct, labor administration, and shortages on Occupation projects. It also includes a substantial report on Imperial Household property and detailed studies of press and radio unions and coal miners.
interest: Translations, meeting records, and occupation directives reveal how Japanese workers, officials, and U.S. authorities contested postwar labor policy.
